description:
## What

New workspace crate `pkix-policy-oscal`. Std-only. Consumes OSCAL Profile JSON (NIST OSCAL v1.2.2 schema) and produces a configured `LintRunner` containing only the workspace Lints selected by the Profile.

Sibling adapter to pkix-policy-zlint and pkix-policy-pkilint, but architecturally different: no subprocess, no external tool dependency. Pure JSON parse + Lint-impl lookup + LintRunner construction.

## Scope

- Parse OSCAL Profile JSON per NIST OSCAL v1.2.2 schema (vendored under specs/oscal-v1.2.2/)
- Extract Control IDs from Profile's imports / merge / modify sections
- Map Control IDs to workspace `Lint` impls via the `Lint::id()` field
- Construct a `LintRunner` carrying only the selected Lints
- Surface OSCAL Profile parse errors with useful context (path, expected types)

## Reuse from pkix-lint

pkix-lint/src/oscal/* already contains OSCAL parsing primitives (parse.rs, catalog.rs, profile.rs). This crate reuses those types. Some pkix-lint internals likely need promotion to public API behind the existing 'oscal' feature flag. Specifically:

- Whatever serde types pkix-lint uses for OSCAL Profile representation
- Helper functions for Profile import resolution

Decide at implementation time: should pkix-policy-oscal depend on pkix-lint with feature 'oscal' enabled, or should pkix-lint's OSCAL types move to a more neutral home (workspace-internal helper crate)? Probably the former — pkix-lint already owns OSCAL emit and the types belong with the emit code.

## Open shape decisions (defer to implementation)

- OSCAL Profile features supported: import-only? import + modify (alters/adds control properties)? import + modify + merge?
- Behavior when Profile references a Control ID that has no corresponding workspace Lint impl: error / warn / silently ignore?
- LintRunner config richness: just select-lints? Also override severity? Apply per-control parameters from OSCAL?
- Does this crate's API admit caching the parse → LintRunner step? Non-negotiable #6 says yes; LintRunner is already Clone+Send+Sync, so caching a configured runner across many cert validations should be straightforward.

## Cross-references

- PKIX-jy95.5 (decision that filed this crate)
- PKIX-9vnx (shipped OSCAL emit/parse code in pkix-lint/src/oscal/*; this crate reuses parse primitives)
- AGENTS.md non-negotiable #5 (three-mode policy-class model; OSCAL named as one optional adapter)
- AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 (cache-friendly types; LintRunner caching for parsed Profiles)
- specs/oscal-v1.2.2/ (NIST schema reference)

## Out of scope

- Implementing OSCAL Catalog support (this crate is for Profile JSON; Catalogs are emit-only via pkix-lint).
- Generic OSCAL Profile composition algebra beyond what's needed to extract selected Control IDs.
- OSCAL emit (already shipped in pkix-lint/src/oscal/emit.rs).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Crate exists in workspace Cargo.toml as a published library
- [ ] Depends on pkix-lint with feature 'oscal' enabled
- [ ] Public API: parse_profile(json) -> Result<Profile, ParseError>; build_runner(profile, lint_registry) -> Result<LintRunner, BuildError>
- [ ] ParseError + BuildError satisfy non-negotiable #6
- [ ] Cargo feature 'serde' enables Serialize/Deserialize derives on the public types
- [ ] Test fixtures: at least one valid OSCAL Profile JSON + several invalid variants exercising error paths
- [ ] Doctest example: load a Profile, configure a LintRunner, run on a cert
- [ ] CHANGELOG + AGENTS.md inventory entry
title: Create pkix-policy-oscal crate (consume OSCAL Profile JSON to configure LintRunner)
